question: Extraction returns `employer`, `works at` and `is employed by` for the same kind of fact across documents. What is the most direct fix?
options: Put the ontology in the prompt (allowed types and relations with their source and target types) and reject anything outside it
Merge the three relations later by hand
explanation: Schema-guided extraction gives the model your vocabulary, and validation enforces it. A bigger model still invents names when it is not told which ones to use.

question: A document's extraction has 12 valid relations and one relation with an unknown type. What should the pipeline do?
options: Discard the whole document and retry until every relation is valid
Accept all 13 relations, since the model saw the text
Accept the 12 valid relations and log the invalid one with its document and reason
Stop the pipeline so a human can look
explanation: Validate per item. Throwing away good facts wastes the call, accepting bad ones corrupts the graph, and the rejection log shows patterns worth fixing.

question: Your graph has nodes "Acme Corp.", "ACME Corporation" and "Acme" (the company) and a product also called "Acme". What should entity resolution produce?
options: Four nodes, since the strings differ
Two nodes: one Organization with the three spellings as aliases, and one separate Product
Three nodes, one per distinct normalized string
explanation: Normalization and aliases merge spelling variants; the type guard keeps a product and a company apart even when their names match.

question: A source document is retracted for containing false claims. Which design lets you remove its facts cleanly?
options: Re-extracting the whole corpus from scratch
Provenance: every entity and relation lists the documents that asserted it, so you remove that source and delete facts left with no source
Asking the model which facts came from that document
Lowering the confidence of every fact
explanation: Provenance makes facts traceable and reversible. It also supports citations and counts of supporting evidence.
